title: Floquet time-convolutionless master equation for non-Markovian driven quantum systems
authors: Pietro Follia, Heinz-Peter Breuer, Bassano Vacchini
abstract: We study the dynamics of open quantum systems driven by an external time-periodic force. Combining Floquet theory and the time-convolutionless projection operator technique we derive a time-local quantum master equation which exactly takes into account the periodic driving, while treating the system-environment interaction within second order in the coupling strength without performing the Markov approximation. The resulting equation of motion for the reduced density matrix is called Floquet time-convolutionless master equation. Employing the example of the driven spin-boson system, we demonstrate that this master equation is capable of describing strong non-Markovian effects, while yielding the Floquet-Lindblad master equation in the Markovian limit. A characteristic feature of memory effects in such driven dissipative systems is the emergence of sharp peaks of the trace-distance based non-Markovianity measure as a function of the driving amplitude, which can be traced back to quasienergy crossings leading to almost decoherence-protected subspaces through a quasienergy-induced dissipative decoupling mechanism.
summary: The paper develops the Floquet time-convolutionless master equation to model open quantum systems under periodic driving while retaining full memory effects. By applying this formalism to the spin-boson model, the authors show that non-Markovianity exhibits sharp peaks precisely when quasienergy degeneracies occur. This work offers a rigorous theoretical tool for understanding how coherent spectral features dictate dissipative dynamics.
main_problem: The primary goal is deriving a time-local quantum master equation that accurately describes the non-Markovian dynamics of open quantum systems subjected to external, periodic driving forces.
main_result: The authors derive the Floquet time-convolutionless (TCL) master equation, demonstrating it captures strong non-Markovian effects characterized by sharp peaks in non-Markovianity at quasienergy crossings.
method: The methodology combines Floquet theory with the time-convolutionless projection operator technique to achieve a time-local description without resorting to the Markov approximation.
model_or_system: The study uses an open quantum system model, exemplified by the driven spin-boson system (a two-level system coupled to a bath of harmonic oscillators). The dynamics are governed by periodically time-dependent Hamiltonians.
key_observables: Non-Markovianity measure (trace-distance based), quasienergies ($\epsilon_n$), and the evolution of the reduced density matrix components (Bloch vector $\mathbf{x}(t)$).
important_parameters: Driving frequency ($\omega$), coupling strength, bath spectral density parameters ($\alpha, \Lambda,  eta$), and the driving amplitude.
main_assumptions: The derivation is perturbative, restricted to second order in the coupling strength. It also assumes an initial factorized state for the system-environment interaction.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate sharp peaks of non-Markovianity as a function of driving amplitude, linked to quasienergy crossings; they also show persistent trace distance revivals in the undriven case when $\epsilon=0$.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the general Floquet-TCL master equation. It then analyzes specific regimes (undriven, RWA circular driving) and focuses heavily on the degenerate quasienergy limit ($\epsilon=0$), providing explicit analytical forms for time evolution coefficients.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, non-Markovian framework for analyzing driven quantum systems, directly linking spectral properties (quasienergy crossings) to memory effects in dissipation, which is crucial for understanding engineered quantum dynamics.
